title: Write user stories with acceptance criteria
summary: User stories describe who needs something and why, so the team builds for a real need. Acceptance criteria say exactly when a story is done, so everyone agrees what to build and how to test it.

beginner: Break each roadmap item (epic) into small pieces of value a user would notice. Each story should be small enough to finish in a few days.
Write each story as: 'As a [type of user], I want [to do something] so that [I get this benefit].' Use a real user group from your research, not just 'user'.

Under each story, add 3 to 6 acceptance criteria. Write them as checks that are either met or not, for example 'It's done when the user can see their reference number', or as 'Given... when... then...'.
Include criteria for errors and edge cases (what happens if the user enters something wrong) and for accessibility (for example, 'works using only a keyboard').
Go through the stories with your engineers and tester before they are planned into work. Their questions will show you what is missing.
Agree a team 'definition of ready': what a story needs before work starts, such as clear criteria, designs attached and dependencies known.
intermediate: Split epics into thin, user-visible stories that each fit within a few days.
Write the stories against real user groups, with testable acceptance criteria covering errors, edge cases and accessibility.
Refine them with engineering and QA before planning, and attach designs.
Agree and apply a definition of ready.
experienced: Keep stories small, valuable to users and independent where possible.
Make acceptance criteria testable, covering unhappy paths and accessibility.
Refine stories with the team, and attach designs and dependencies.
Agree a definition of ready and use it.

canDelegateTo.task: Draft stories and acceptance criteria for the PM to review
Add edge cases and test scenarios to the acceptance criteria
Write the user-facing text the stories need
Split stories so they can be built and released independently

toolExamples.jira: Set a description template for the Story work type with sections for the story, acceptance criteria and design links. Link each story to its epic.
toolExamples.azure-devops: Use the User Story work item. Put the criteria in the Acceptance Criteria field so they show up in test planning.
toolExamples.linear: Use an issue template with headings for the story and acceptance criteria.
toolExamples.figma: Paste a link to the exact frame each story covers, not the whole file.
toolExamples.claude: Paste a draft story and ask for missing edge cases and error states. You decide which ones belong in this story.
toolExamples.copilot: Ask it to suggest Given/When/Then criteria from your story, then check them with your tester.

definitionOfDone: Each story names a real user group and a clear benefit
Each story has testable acceptance criteria, including errors and accessibility
Stories reviewed with engineering and QA before planning
Definition of ready agreed by the team
pitfalls: Writing technical tasks and calling them user stories
Stories too big to finish in a sprint or a few days
Criteria that describe the screen layout rather than the outcome
